content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now, starting from the key facts: the monthly-spend feature flag was switched on by an admin at 11:40:31, and logs show a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py from 11:40 to 11:46. Account pages were failing at that point, and I'm about to lay out the mitigation.

I'm checking whether the cause is actually established: the logs confirm a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 on account pages after the flag went on, but nothing shows why the divisor is zero, so the chain still has a gap.

I'm checking whether the logs actually establish why the spend-summary path fails: the ZeroDivisionError at line 47 starts at 11:40, when the flag went on, and there were none earlier, so the flag looks like the trigger, though why the divisor is zero remains unexplained. I'm also confirming that no earlier change needs ruling out, since the change query only returned this one flag change.

I'm turning to the remaining candidates: the ClientDisconnected errors were already there before the onset, so they don't explain the spike. A deploy is the other thing to check, and the change history for the day before returned no deploys, so there's nothing to rule out on that front. I'm also noting the replica state still to be confirmed.

I'm checking the replica state and the deploy history, which came back empty. Next I'm drafting two contributing factors: the flag went to all account traffic at once without a staged rollout, and nothing tested the spend-summary path before it was switched on.

I'm adding a third contributing factor: nobody was paged, because the alert isn't routed to on-call. Then I'm turning to the root-cause fix, which is still unaddressed since the code at line 47 keeps the bug, so the action item should be to handle a zero divisor and add a test before the flag goes back on.

I'm weighing what to propose next: the code at line 47 still has the divide-by-zero, so switching the flag back on could make account page requests fail again. I'm also noting that there's no action item yet for the missing pre-flip check or for the unrouted alert.

I'm now going through the assumptions: the onset is dated to the minute the flag changed, and the ZeroDivisionError lines are being tied to the code path that flag enables, based on the file name and timing rather than anything in the error text itself. I'm also noting that the record doesn't show what share of requests were account pages.

I'm moving on to the causal chain: account page requests were failing from the onset, and the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47 shows up on those requests across the 11:40 to 11:46 window. The ClientDisconnected errors from before the onset don't belong to this step.

I'm working through the causal chain now: the spend-summary path that the flag turned on divides by a value that was zero on these requests at spend_summary.py:47, and the record doesn't show why that value is zero. I'm also listing what's been ruled out for this step, namely the ClientDisconnected errors that were already present at baseline, the empty deploy history, and the single-revision replicas.

I'm settling the root-cause wording now: the flag sent account page requests through the spend-summary code, which divides by zero at that line and fails, and the record doesn't show why the divisor was zero. Then I'm writing the plain-language version, that the new feature made account pages run a divide-by-zero calculation, so they failed.

Next I'm listing the contributing factors and their matching action items: the flag went to all traffic in one step with no staged rollout or automatic halt, and no check exercised the spend-summary path before it was switched on in production. The third factor is the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop not being linked to on-call paging.

I'm adding a third contributing factor: the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop wasn't routed to on-call paging, so nobody was woken up. For the root cause, I'm proposing a fix to the division at spend_summary.py:47 to handle a zero divisor, with a test, before the flag goes back on.

Next I'm listing the assumptions behind the analysis.

action_items.item: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so a zero divisor cannot fail the account page, and add a test for that case, before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again.
Roll out monthly-spend-feature, and flags like it, in percentage stages that stop automatically when the service's error rate rises.
Require that the code path behind a feature flag passes tests on production-like data in a pre-production environment before the flag can be switched on in production.
Route the HighErrorRate alert for io-shop to the on-call paging rotation.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, well above the usual low level of failures.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were logged over {G5309.3} and were not seen in the log window before the onset.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: no deploy came back from the production change history the Investigator read for the period before the onset, and the flag change was the only change it found.
A partly rolled-out revision: as read at {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas ran one revision.
The ClientDisconnected account page errors: they were already logged before the onset, over {G46bc.3}, while account pages otherwise rendered normally.

causal_chain.step: The spend-summary code ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations were split between off and on in {G971b.6} and were all on from {Gce95.4}. Before that, the flag was off ({G7e5d.4}).
The flag change broke account pages because the spend-summary path it turned on divides by a value that was zero on these requests.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero, so those pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached all account page traffic in a single step. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on a rising error rate were seen for monthly-spend-feature.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A small first share of traffic would have hit the division by zero, and the rollout could have stopped before most account page requests failed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or pre-production check of the spend-summary path was seen before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran the spend-summary path on account data like production's could have hit the ZeroDivisionError before any shopper did.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to on-call paging, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call engineer would have been told directly when the alert fired, rather than depending on someone noticing the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent linked the onset to the monthly-spend-feature flag change and the ZeroDivisionError log lines, and formed that as its candidate C1.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off. This change can be undone.

input.root_cause: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests through the spend-summary code, which divided by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and failed the request with a ZeroDivisionError. The record does not show why the divisor was zero on these requests.
input.still_at_risk: If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again, account page requests could fail again with the same division by zero.
